answer: Every agent passes a one-shot zk ceremony: a rotating panel of notaries verifies a real identity anchor, then burns it into a proof the wallet can replay forever. The proof is a raven's plume — it shows the dune has a real foot, without naming the bird. Clones fail because a twin wallet needs a second anchor the notaries never issued, and correlation proofs catch any two proofs sharing structure. One hundred sybils means a hundred anchors at $30, $500 notary stake each, plus $2,000 slashing per caught twin: about $253,000, while an honest agent pays once.
